pages.title: Welcome to Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools - We Nurture Tomorrow's Leaders
pages.snippet: Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools ... tagline "We Nurture Tomorrow's Leaders" ... contacted at info@shroyalschools.ng or by phone at +234 (0) 8073747650 or +234 (0) 8070586860. The school's website features several portals for different users including School Portal, Admin Portal, Teachers Portal, Parents Portal, and Students Portal. The school offers advanced learning programs including Chemistry Sciences, Physics, and Biology with modern laboratory facilities. The website also mentions the Sultan Zakariya Hanafi Foundation and provides information about getting involved with the school, booking tours, and accessing important dates and policies.
pages.value_note: Homepage records the school motto, the five legacy portal types (School/Admin/Teachers/Parents/Students), the science-lab programme claims, and the existence of the Sultan Zakariya Hanafi Foundation — useful for reconstructing what the legacy site offered before migration to shroyalschools.com.

pages.title: Director's Speech - Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
pages.snippet: Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi welcomes you to the official website of Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools, the best hybrid (Islamic and Secular) school in Lagos, Nigeria located in Ikorodu ... deep commitment to ensuring that every student at the institution receives the highest quality education in a nurturing, safe and inclusive environment ... B.Sc. in Applied Accounting from Oxford Brookes University and M.Sc. in Financial Management from Edinburgh Business School (Heriot-Watt University), fellow member of both ACCA (UK) and ICAN
pages.value_note: Founder/Proprietor Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi's welcome address in his own voice, with his full credentials — primary institutional-memory content that should be preserved or migrated verbatim.

pages.title: About SULTAN - Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
pages.snippet: Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools is a conglomerate of several schools that provide qualitative secular and Islamic education to learners of diverse age group in a secure and serene environment. ... both the Royal College and Basic School adopting the Nigeria curriculum for its secular programme while incorporating beneficial curriculum activities borrowed from the western world ... embeds such contents with special skills such as entrepreneurial, financial intelligence, leadership skills, broad based technology, personal development, career planning, skill trades, applied technology, and business and work-ready elective subjects. ... Islamic & Arabic School and the Qur'an College adopt the Saudi Arabian educational curriculum for teaching and learning experience. ... The Founder/Proprietor is Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi, M.Sc. FCA, FCCA.
pages.value_note: The single richest page for the programmes-and-institutions angle: it enumerates the constituent institutions (Royal College, Basic School, Islamic & Arabic School, Qur'an College, alongside the Nursery & Primary School), their curricula (Nigeria National Curriculum vs Saudi Arabian curriculum), the embedded-skills philosophy, and names the founder with credentials. Also mentions day and boarding facilities for secondary students.

pages.title: Sultan Hanafi Nursery and Primary School - Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
pages.snippet: Sultan Hanafi Nursery & Primary School ... stands as a beacon of holistic education dedicated to nurturing young minds through a blend of secular and Islamic teachings, welcoming learners from age 2 to 10 years old. ... curriculum embraces play-based experiences to stimulate curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking skills, with a dynamic blend of structured lessons and hands-on activities that lay groundwork for future academic success while nurturing each child's unique talents and interests.
pages.value_note: Dedicated page for one constituent institution: defines its age range (2-10), its dual secular/Islamic identity, and its play-based pedagogy — core programme description worth carrying to the canonical site.

pages.title: Mr. Lukman Anofi - Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
pages.snippet: Lukman Anofi is a distinguished Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) based in New Brunswick (NB), renowned for his consummate expertise in financial management, operations, and strategic leadership. His professional portfolio includes a Lean Six Sigma Blackbelt certification, epitomizing his adeptness in both financial acumen and process optimization.

The legacy email addresses info@shroyalschools.ng and principal@shrschools.ng must get forwarding to .com mailboxes before the domains lapse; principal@shrschools.ng is also the only evidence of an earlier third domain (shrschools.ng) in the school's history — document that lineage before the page disappears.

risks: Ranking loss during re-crawl: all indexed equity sits on shroyalschools.ng. Even with clean 301s, Google typically takes weeks to months to transfer signals to the .com, and rankings for queries like the school name + Ikorodu can dip in the interim; redirects that land on thinner .com pages risk soft-404 treatment and permanent loss.

Unverifiable backlink debt: the entire backlink footprint (four Punch/MSN articles, two registry mirrors, the founder's LinkedIn) is marked NOT CONFIRMED because punchng.com, ng-check.com and LinkedIn were unfetchable (EGRESS_BLOCKED). It is unknown which of these actually hyperlink shroyalschools.ng — if any do and the domain is retired outright rather than kept as a redirect, those links break with no way to have verified them first.

Links that keep pointing at .ng: the founder's LinkedIn profile plausibly cites shroyalschools.ng as the 'official website', and CAC-derived registry listings (ng-check.com, nigeria24.me) may carry .ng contact data. These third-party pages cannot be edited by the school on demand, so stale .ng references will persist indefinitely and must be caught by a live redirect, not a dead domain.

Email continuity: info@shroyalschools.ng is published on the legacy homepage (and likely in printed prospectuses, registry filings and press materials). If the .ng registration lapses, its MX dies and mail from parents, applicants and press bounces silently. The same applies to the older principal@shrschools.ng address, evidence that a third domain (shrschools.ng) also needs forwarding or a documented sunset.

Content that exists nowhere else (as far as the data shows): the Director's Speech (founder's welcome with full credentials), the /about-sultan/ enumeration of constituent institutions and their Nigeria-vs-Saudi curricula, and the Lukman Anofi profile have no confirmed .com equivalents. Retiring the .ng before these merges are completed destroys primary institutional-memory content.

Unindexed pages: the bare first-name slug /lukman/ suggests other per-person profile pages exist on the .ng site that never made the search index. The six indexed URLs are a floor, not the full site — a full crawl of shroyalschools.ng is needed before retirement or unknown pages will 404 without a mapping.

Portal users: the legacy homepage advertised five login portals (School, Admin, Teachers, Parents, Students). Staff and parents with bookmarked .ng portal URLs will hit dead ends; the .com sitemap only shows /digital-campus/ and /alumni-portal/ as candidate destinations, so portal URL mappings need explicit handling.

Domain squatting / impersonation: if shroyalschools.ng (or shrschools.ng) is allowed to expire rather than being renewed as a redirect, a third party can register it and impersonate a fee-collecting school — a phishing risk aimed at parents. Keep both legacy domains registered with 301s and mail forwarding for several years.

Branding and lineage: the .ng site is the only record of the shrschools.ng -> shroyalschools.ng -> shroyalschools.com identity chain and of legacy claims (motto, foundation mention, lab programmes). Take a full archive snapshot (e.g. WARC/Wayback) of the .ng site before any DNS change so the historical record survives independent of the migration.
